In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic structure of the superconducting cuprates and related compounds.
the electronic and magnetic properties of the high-Tc superconducting oxides.
the role of spin-orbit coupling in the formation and properties of polarons in the high temperature superconductor, YBCO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed spectral changes in the YBCO are due to a combination of charge polarization, and spin-orbit effects.

the observed white line intensity ratio anomalies are due to the charge polarization effects, and the white line intensity anomalies are a direct spectroscopic evidence for the polarons in the partially occupied spin-orbital states in YBCO.
the white-line intensities in YBCO are not only due to the final state effects but also to the core-hole screening and charge polarization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cu and Ba atoms in YBCO have partially occupied spin-orbital states, with a charge distribution that is different from the ionic charge distribution.
the polarons in YBCO are the charge carriers, and the charge transfer is the mechanism of high temperature superconductivity.
